BETWEEN:-
 KASHIRAM S/O SUNDARLAL, AGED ABOUT 35 YEARS,
 OCCUPATION:
SARPANCH GRAM PANCHAYAT R/O  YENASH TAH MULTAI TAHSIL AND DISTRICT BETUL  (MADHYA PRADESH)

(BY SHRI PRAKASH GUPTA - ADVOCATE )
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION AMLA DISTRICT BETUL (MADHYA PRADESH)
 .

(BY SHRI VIVEK LAKHERA - GOVT. ADVOCATE )
 (BY SHRI RAJENDRA YADAV - ADVOCATE FOR OBJECTOR)
This application coming on for admission this day,

the c  following:
 ORDER

This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.77/2024 dated 07.02.2024 registered at Police Station, Amla District, Betul for the offence punishable under sections 450, 506 and 376(1)
of IPC.
2.

Learned counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant is the Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat - Yenash, Tehsil - Multai District Betul and on account of faction rivalry the present applicant has been falsely implicated.
Learned counsel contends that the prosecution story is ill-founded.
As per prosecution, the incident has taken place on 01-01-2024, whereas the FIR has been lodged on 07-02-2024.
The attempt to submit explanation for delayed lodging of the FIR is also unsustainable.
Inasmuch as the delay is of more than one month, entire prosecution story is suspicious and doubtful.
It is thus, contended by the counsel that the applicant who is suffering incarceration since 09-02-2024 deserves to be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail and submitted that the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 164 of CrPC reflects that the alleged offence has been committed by the applicant.
There are direct allegations against the applicant, and thus, no case for grant of bail is made out.

4. Learned counsel for the objector has supported the submissions advanced on behalf of the State and submitted that the applicant being the Sarpanch of the Gram Panchayat, is an influential person and there is likelihood of tampering with the evidence by him.
Thus, submits that the application deserves to be dismissed.

5. Having heard submissions advanced on behalf of the parties, perusal of the record reflects that it is undisputed that in regard to the incident dated 01- 01-2024, the FIR has been lodged on 07-02-2024.
It is also evident that the MLC report prima facie does not implicate the present applicant and the prosecutrix undisputedly is a married lady.
Therefore, taking into consideration the totality of the circumstances, this Court deems it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant- Kashiram shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
8.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
Certified copy as per rules.
